violated_contract: Ending capture, cancelling its pending permission request or failing its startup must release the native audio session as well as the engine. A stopped timer is not evidence that microphone-session ownership ended; activating audio before validating a delayed permission answer can resurrect ownership after Stop.
canonical_prevention: Keep permission checking side-effect free, validate the original start generation before activating audio, and route Stop and failed-start cleanup through the same resource-release method. Stop the tap/engine before deactivating AVAudioSession. A native SDK probe runs the actual WatchAudioRecorderViewModel with injected permission and audio-session I/O and verifies late/cancelled/ABA permission answers, failed activation, terminal Stop and repeated Stop. Physical microphone behavior remains a separate acceptance lane.
